taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Older Texas sources may file Penstemon under Scrophulariaceae; current project taxonomy uses Plantaginaceae.

evidence: Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County legacy Scrophulariaceae index includes three Penstemon cobaea specimens.
Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed county treatment for Penstemon cobaea.
Kerr County — the published vascular flora of Kerr Wildlife Management Area lists Penstemon cobaea with voucher JS 10550.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Purola Preserve lists P. cobaea among introduced species from nearby Hill Country sources, so that Hays record is not used as native-county proof.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with flower size and the leaf node. Prairie penstemon has enormous pale lavender-to-white flowers, usually about 35–55 mm long, and opposite serrate stem leaves that are sessile and often fused across the node. The calyx and inflorescence are glandular-hairy, and the throat is abruptly inflated.
diagnostic_traits: short-lived perennial with several stout stems from a perennial crown/rhizome
opposite cauline leaves, sessile and often connate across the stem
leaf blades broad and usually sharply serrate
corolla very large, white to lavender, with darker nectar guides
corolla tube abruptly enlarged below the midpoint

confusers.separator: P. triflorus usually has smaller 25–35 mm pink/red flowers; P. cobaea has much larger abruptly inflated pale flowers and broader serrate leaves.
P. tenuis has much smaller 10–14 mm lavender/violet flowers and favors wet alluvial/coastal prairie habitats.
P. baccharifolius is a woody-based subshrub with small thick leathery toothed leaves and red tubular flowers from limestone crevices.

installation_guardrail: May install under the user's blanket approval because strict PASS is complete.
